comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
To those struggling with this issue, a workaround that was sufficient for my usecase:

Check if your instance root volume is using the maximum allocated IOPS. For example, with AWS EC2 EBS-backed volumes, granting the volume sufficient IOPS overhead outright made this issue go away almost entirely. We noticed that this issue was happening when during the booting of EKS nodes (when attempting to pull many images at once). IOPS was hovering at roughly 99% capacity every time this occurred.

We have implemented a workaround by adding it into our internal operator to detect the issue and delete the pod with this condition instantly without waiting for the normal life-cycle (iiuc, it depends on backoff limit, before the pod is deleted and rescheduled).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Based on the PR information, _will fix_ seems like an invalid statement - doesn't that just move the error somewhere else? We also increased IOPs and saw reduction in errors, but these are extremely beefy AWS instances and some expensive disks to back them to handle this failure case. As this is the most liked bug in containerd doesn't that perhaps imply the context deadline should have a longer default to help mitigate for the community? Or backoff and retry automatically? Admittedly I'm not remotely familiar with this codebase and won't pretend to be an expert, just spewing ideas.
